data.name: AppStatements_Title
data.comment: Page title and tooltip of its button: the statements a running .NET app sends to the database

data.name: AppStatements_ListFailed
data.value: The running .NET apps cannot be listed: {0}
data.comment: {0}: error message of the system

data.name: AppStatements_ReadFailed
data.comment: {0}: error message of the system

data.name: AppStatements_App
data.comment: Section heading: the traced .NET app

data.name: AppStatements_ProcessesHint
data.value: .NET apps running on this computer under your user. Start your app (debugging in Visual Studio, dotnet run …) and attach to it – it needs no change, EF Core 7 or later shows where each statement comes from.

data.name: AppStatements_ShowTooling
data.comment: {0}: number of hidden processes (MSBuild, compiler server …)

data.name: AppStatements_ShowToolingTitle
data.value: MSBuild nodes, the compiler server, the dotnet CLI and Visual Studio’s helpers run on .NET too – they are hidden because they are never the app to look at

data.name: AppStatements_Refresh
data.comment: Button: read the list of running apps again

data.name: AppStatements_NoProcesses
data.value: No .NET app found. Start your app and refresh.

data.name: AppStatements_ColumnApp
data.comment: Column heading: process name

data.name: AppStatements_ColumnEnvironment
data.comment: Column heading: value of -environment=… on the app's command line

data.name: AppStatements_ColumnStarted
data.comment: Column heading: when the process started

data.name: AppStatements_Attach
data.comment: Button: start reading the app's statements

data.name: AppStatements_Detach
data.comment: Button: stop reading the app's statements (the recording stays)

data.name: AppStatements_Clear
data.comment: Button: forget what was recorded so far, the trace goes on

data.name: AppStatements_ClearTitle
data.value: Forget what was recorded so far, e.g. before the step you want to look at

data.name: AppStatements_Pause
data.comment: Button: stay attached, but leave out new statements

data.name: AppStatements_PauseTitle
data.value: Stay attached, but leave out new statements until you resume – the recording so far stays

data.name: AppStatements_Resume
data.comment: Button: record new statements again after a pause

data.name: AppStatements_StatusPaused
data.value: paused – new statements are left out

data.name: AppStatements_Environment
data.comment: Label before the app's environment name

data.name: AppStatements_StatusAttaching
data.value: attaching – waiting for the first statement …

data.name: AppStatements_Connection
data.comment: Label: the FerretSharp connection the app works on

data.name: AppStatements_ByEnvironment
data.comment: How the connection was found

data.name: AppStatements_ByDataSource
data.comment: How the connection was found

data.name: AppStatements_Chosen
data.comment: How the connection was found: picked by the user

data.name: AppStatements_NoConnection
data.value: None found yet (it is known with the first statement) – or choose one:

data.name: AppStatements_ChooseConnectionTitle
data.value: The connection to the database the app works on: statements are looked up and opened there

data.name: AppStatements_ChangeConnection
data.comment: Button: choose another connection

data.name: AppStatements_RememberEnvironment
data.comment: {0}: the app's environment name; it is saved as the connection's app environment

data.name: AppStatements_RememberFailed
data.value: The app environment could not be saved: {0}
data.comment: {0}: error message of the system

data.name: AppStatements_Overview
data.comment: Section heading: statements grouped by where they come from (LINQ, lazy loading …)

data.name: AppStatements_SummaryOne
data.comment: {0}: number of statements run; {1}: their total time; {2}: time of day the recording started

data.name: AppStatements_SummaryOther
data.comment: {0}: number of statements run; {1}: their total time; {2}: time of day the recording started

data.name: AppStatements_Waiting
data.value: No statement yet – use your app.

data.name: AppStatements_ColumnOrigin
data.comment: Column heading: where a statement comes from (LINQ, lazy loading, raw SQL …)

data.name: AppStatements_ColumnCount
data.comment: Column heading: how often

data.name: AppStatements_ColumnTime
data.comment: Column heading: total time, running and reading the rows

data.name: AppStatements_ColumnRows
data.comment: Column heading: rows read or changed

data.name: AppStatements_FilterTitle
data.value: Show only the statements of this origin

data.name: AppStatements_OnlyOrigin
data.comment: {0}: an origin (LINQ, Lazy Loading …); button that removes this filter

data.name: AppStatements_Truncated
data.value: More than {0} different statements: further ones count only by origin.
data.comment: {0}: the limit

data.name: AppStatements_MoreRows
data.value: … and {0} more – filter by origin or sort to see others.
data.comment: {0}: number of statements not shown

data.name: AppStatements_ErrorsBadge
data.comment: {0}: how often the statement failed

data.name: AppStatements_RepeatedTitle
data.value: Ran up to {0} times within {1} s in one DbContext – often an N+1 problem
data.comment: {0}: most runs seen within the window; {1}: the window in seconds

data.name: AppStatements_RepeatedLazy
data.value: Ran up to {0} times within {1} s in one DbContext by lazy loading of “{2}” – an N+1 problem: load the navigation together with the query (Include) or for all rows at once.
data.comment: {0}: most runs within the window; {1}: the window in seconds; {2}: name of the navigation

data.name: AppStatements_RepeatedLoop
data.value: Ran up to {0} times within {1} s in one DbContext – probably once per row in a loop (N+1): one query for all rows is usually much faster.
data.comment: {0}: most runs within the window; {1}: the window in seconds

data.name: AppStatements_DetailCountOne
data.comment: {0}: number of runs; {1}: total time

data.name: AppStatements_DetailCountOther
data.comment: {0}: number of runs; {1}: total time

data.name: AppStatements_LookUp
data.comment: Button: read V$SQL figures and plan of the statement

data.name: AppStatements_LookUpTitle
data.value: Figures and plan of the statement from V$SQL of the app’s connection (connects if needed)

data.name: AppStatements_NotConnected
data.value: The connection could not be opened.

data.name: AppStatements_LookupTimedOut
data.value: The database did not answer in time.

data.name: AppStatements_NotInPool
data.value: The statement is not (or no longer) in the database’s shared pool – the app may work on another database, or it was aged out.

data.name: AppStatements_RowsProcessed
data.comment: Label: rows processed by all executions

data.name: AppStatements_Elapsed
data.comment: Label: elapsed time of all executions

data.name: AppStatements_InstanceWide
data.value: The figures count every session of the database that ran the statement, not only this app.

data.name: AppStatements_NoActualFigures
data.value: The plan has only estimates: measured rows and times per step are there only if the statement ran with statistics (GATHER_PLAN_STATISTICS or STATISTICS_LEVEL = ALL). For them, open it in the SQL editor and show the actual plan.

data.name: AppStatements_OriginOther
data.comment: Origin: migrations, value generators

data.name: AppStatements_OriginUnknown
data.comment: Origin: EF did not say (EF Core before 7)
